comment:
The gallery-marker change introduces a trust-boundary regression in the source path reviewed at `8a2e927`.

## A theme can declare itself trusted

[`theme_is_gallery_trusted()`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/8a2e9276a354e6cc27507c977978113a2241a57d/bin/omarchy-theme-set#L253-L283) reads `.omarchy-theme.yml` from the cloned repository itself. Any theme author can add `gallery: true`, which bypasses the entire installed-theme denylist. The installer accepts repository URLs without checking gallery membership or obtaining separate authorization to run theme code.

Source-level comparison for a git-cloned theme shipping authored `hyprland.lua`:

| Repository contents | Before | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| No gallery marker | Lua stripped | Lua stripped |
| Repo-authored `gallery: true` marker | Lua stripped | Lua staged unchanged |

Templates leave an already-staged file intact, and [Hyprland's setup loads the current theme's Lua module](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/8a2e9276a354e6cc27507c977978113a2241a57d/default/hypr/omarchy.lua#L22-L23). Symlink checks do not prevent this path: both the marker and Lua can be ordinary files.

**Impact:** Installing a self-labelled third-party theme can now supply Lua for the compositor to execute, contrary to the documented installed-theme code restriction. The exception also admits terminal configs and `vscode.json`, not just decoration settings.

**Suggested change:** Keep authorization outside repository-controlled metadata. Use separately trusted repository/revision authorization or an explicit informed local opt-in for executable theme files. Alternatively, accept declarative decoration values and generate the Lua locally while retaining the denylist.

**Verified (source inspection):** Marked themes retain authored Lua, while unmarked git themes remain filtered and symlink refusal is retained. This restores the authored-Lua staging path, not decoration for themes that only provide `hyprland.conf`.
